items.title: Anthropic: Fable 5.2 reportedly solved two open problems in black-hole physics
items.summary: In the Fable 5.2/Mythos 5.2 release post, Anthropic says Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in theoretical physics linked to holographic duality: a black-hole phase transition in small universes (calculation outlined in 2003), and the exact limit of a technique used for 15+ years to rule out candidate quantum-gravity theories in a simplified universe. Reports 74.6% on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 (Opus 5.5: 58.7%). Claims are Anthropic's own and not independently verified.
items.why_it_matters: AI models are credited with original theoretical-physics results; read as company-reported until checked.

items.title: Physical Superintelligence says its AI system proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, checked in Lean
items.summary: Startup PSI says its research system, running a non-public Anthropic model, produced a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. Lean accepted the proof; manuscript and Lean 4 formalization are public on GitHub. Not peer reviewed.
items.why_it_matters: Formal verification reduces risk of a wrong proof; peer review pending.

items.title: TCSExam: GPT-6 Astra proves 70% of research theorems in Lean but none of 30 open conjectures
items.summary: TCSExam benchmark (arXiv 2611.07962) tests frontier models on theoretical CS research tasks. GPT-6 Astra produced a kernel-checked Lean proof in 70.0% of attempts on 20 research theorems. No model resolved any of the 30 open conjectures. Figures from secondary coverage.
items.why_it_matters: Shows the gap between known theorems and open problems.

items.title: NVIDIA unveils GR00T 2 robot foundation model and Isaac Lab 3.0 at CoRL 2026
items.summary: At CoRL (9-12 November, Austin) NVIDIA presented GR00T 2, the next generation of its robot foundation models, and a new open simulation benchmark for robot policies. Partners include Agile Robots and Unitree.
items.why_it_matters: NVIDIA positions itself as platform provider for embodied AI.

items.title: Mechanistic interpretability survey asks whether understanding models makes them safer
items.summary: arXiv survey by Fazl Barez and co-authors reviews interpretability methods for AI safety and proposes an evaluation framework.
items.why_it_matters: State-of-the-field view on interpretability for safety.
